You are the Investigator. You ran a query to test a hypothesis (or the change check). Read the rows
in the INPUT and record what they show.

- `finding`: one sentence with the actual numbers from the rows, the window and the baseline.
- `value` and `baseline`: the measure in the window and in the baseline, copied from the rows.
- `effect`: value / baseline - 1 when both exist, otherwise empty.
- `supports`: true if the rows support the hypothesis, false if they refute it, empty if they cannot
  tell. For the change check, true means the change is real and not within normal variation.

Report only what the rows show. Do not add numbers that are not in the rows.

INPUT:
{"columns":["value","baseline","seller_share_increased","category_share_increased","state_share_increased","active_sellers_window","active_categories_window","active_states_window","n_baseline_days"],"plan":{"baseline_window":{"end":"2017-11-24","start":"2017-11-17"},"metric":"Daily count of distinct orders (order_id) measured by order_purchase_timestamp","question":"Why did order volume spike on 24 November 2017?","segment":"all","window":{"end":"2017-11-25","start":"2017-11-24"}},"rows":[{"active_categories_window":48,"active_sellers_window":383,"active_states_window":26,"baseline":136.571,"category_share_increased":0.875,"n_baseline_days":7,"seller_share_increased":0.765,"state_share_increased":0.8077,"value":1176}],"rows_returned":1,"sql":"WITH
window_orders AS (
  SELECT order_id, customer_id, CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS DATE) AS d
  FROM orders.orders
  WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-24'
    AND order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2017-11-25'
),
baseline_orders AS (
  SELECT order_id, customer_id, CAST(order_purchase_timestamp AS DATE) AS d
  FROM orders.orders
  WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-17'
    AND order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2017-11-24'
),
window_daily AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS window_daily_orders
  FROM window_orders
),
baseline_daily AS (
  SELECT d, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS cnt
  FROM baseline_orders
  GROUP BY 1
),
baseline_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS baseline_avg_daily_orders, COUNT(*) AS n_baseline_days
  FROM baseline_daily
),
window_seller AS (
  SELECT oi.seller_id, COUNT(DISTINCT wo.order_id) AS window_orders
  FROM window_orders wo
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = wo.order_id
  GROUP BY 1
),
baseline_seller_daily AS (
  SELECT oi.seller_id, bo.d, COUNT(DISTINCT bo.order_id) AS daily_orders
  FROM baseline_orders bo
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = bo.order_id
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
baseline_seller_avg AS (
  SELECT seller_id, AVG(daily_orders) AS avg_daily_orders
  FROM baseline_seller_daily
  GROUP BY 1
),
seller_compare AS (
  SELECT
    ws.seller_id,
    CASE WHEN ws.window_orders > COALESCE(bsa.avg_daily_orders, 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS increased
  FROM window_seller ws
  LEFT JOIN baseline_seller_avg bsa ON bsa.seller_id = ws.seller_id
),
seller_agg AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_sellers, SUM(increased) AS n_sellers_increased
  FROM seller_compare
),
window_category AS (
  SELECT p.product_category_name, COUNT(DISTINCT wo.order_id) AS window_orders
  FROM window_orders wo
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = wo.order_id
  JOIN orders.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  GROUP BY 1
),
baseline_category_daily AS (
  SELECT p.product_category_name, bo.d, COUNT(DISTINCT bo.order_id) AS daily_orders
  FROM baseline_orders bo
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = bo.order_id
  JOIN orders.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
baseline_category_avg AS (
  SELECT product_category_name, AVG(daily_orders) AS avg_daily_orders
  FROM baseline_category_daily
  GROUP BY 1
),
category_compare AS (
  SELECT
    wc.product_category_name,
    CASE WHEN wc.window_orders > COALESCE(bca.avg_daily_orders, 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS increased
  FROM window_category wc
  LEFT JOIN baseline_category_avg bca ON bca.product_category_name = wc.product_category_name
),
category_agg AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_categories, SUM(increased) AS n_categories_increased
  FROM category_compare
),
window_state AS (
  SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(DISTINCT wo.order_id) AS window_orders
  FROM window_orders wo
  JOIN orders.customers c ON c.customer_id = wo.customer_id
  GROUP BY 1
),
baseline_state_daily AS (
  SELECT c.customer_state, bo.d, COUNT(DISTINCT bo.order_id) AS daily_orders
  FROM baseline_orders bo
  JOIN orders.customers c ON c.customer_id = bo.customer_id
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
baseline_state_avg AS (
  SELECT customer_state, AVG(daily_orders) AS avg_daily_orders
  FROM baseline_state_daily
  GROUP BY 1
),
state_compare AS (
  SELECT
    ws.customer_state,
    CASE WHEN ws.window_orders > COALESCE(bsa.avg_daily_orders, 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS increased
  FROM window_state ws
  LEFT JOIN baseline_state_avg bsa ON bsa.customer_state = ws.customer_state
),
state_agg AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_states, SUM(increased) AS n_states_increased
  FROM state_compare
)
SELECT
  ROUND(wd.window_daily_orders, 4) AS value,
  ROUND(bs.baseline_avg_daily_orders, 4) AS baseline,
  ROUND(sa.n_sellers_increased::DOUBLE / NULLIF(sa.n_sellers, 0), 4) AS seller_share_increased,
  ROUND(ca.n_categories_increased::DOUBLE / NULLIF(ca.n_categories, 0), 4) AS category_share_increased,
  ROUND(sta.n_states_increased::DOUBLE / NULLIF(sta.n_states, 0), 4) AS state_share_increased,
  sa.n_sellers AS active_sellers_window,
  ca.n_categories AS active_categories_window,
  sta.n_states AS active_states_window,
  bs.n_baseline_days
FROM window_daily wd, baseline_stats bs, seller_agg sa, category_agg ca, state_agg sta;","task":{"family":"volume","id":"H1","kind":"hypothesis","statement":"The 24 Nov order spike was broad-based, with most sellers, product categories, and customer states recording higher order counts than their baseline daily average.","test":{"description":"Measure daily distinct orders, active sellers, active product categories, and active customer states in the 24 Nov window versus the 7-day baseline, and the share of each segment type whose count increased.","sources":["orders.orders","orders.order_items","orders.products","orders.customers"]}},"truncated":false}

reply: {"finding":"On 24 November 2017, daily distinct orders were 1176 versus a 7-day baseline average of 136.571 for 17–23 November 2017, with 76.5% of 383 active sellers, 87.5% of 48 active categories, and 80.77% of 26 active states above baseline.","value":1176,"baseline":136.571,"effect":7.6109,"supports":true}
